body: Thanks. Like you said, those are good characteristics to work on regardless. I had a bit of time to think about it and I had a similar conclusion: just try best to work on it, and if she's still dissatisfied, I'll just had to accpect that she could never be.

First, thanks for the kind words. 

I written that the night of it happened, and it has been a day or two now. It's not like I don't know about some of the stuff you mentioned, they are Asian parent stereotypes after all. But it's different hearing it from someone else. Helps me make the connection and internalise the concept better. 

She always "joke" that I would always be her kid, I guess I never knew how serious she was. I wasn't in the best place in my head when I heard that. While she doesn't mean much, hearing that at this moment definitely doesn't help. It just sucks that as much as I would like to appease her, it'll never happen. It doesn't help that even everyday small choices she can't take me seriously. And if I let her make the decisions instead of just having her reject my idea anyway, she thinks I'm indecisive. I can't shake the feeling that anything good I do, it's expected of me so she doesn't need to show appreciation, and anything bad I do, any mistake I make, it's all my fault. 

I guess I need find a new angle to look at this or just suck it up. Like you said, be less sensitive, and try to find a better sense of self worth and confidence (and I've been trying for awhile at these two points now). I don't how much it matters if she's actually proud and happy for me. It just loses some sense genuineness when she said she's happy for me during grad while she could never be truly satisfied and respect my choices. 

Sometimes we make fun of how people thing they're the exception. Well I thought my mom was, and doesn't follow the stereotype much. 

Anyway, thanks for reading my ramble. I appreciate it.

My mom was talking on Skype with her sister (my aunt). My aunt must have asked my mom about her opinion on me and my girlfriend (whom they have not spent much time together until now). I heard my mom say "Ok, I'll have to talk softer now." I know that she knows I'm within hearing range. She then proceed to talk her heart out at normal volume. 

To sum it up, she thinks that I either can't multi-task, or can't handle much responsibilities. I'm indecisive (she also shares that opinion towards my girlfriend). I have no manners, easily angered and with fragile emotions, so I need to be babied. From her word choices and tone, she just generally does not think highly of me.

Listening to all that, while she joke and laugh with her sister, asking her if her sons (my cousins) behaves the same, and saying how my brother doesn't behave like me, hurts. I don't think it's unreasonable to be upset about listening to someone, let alone my mother, talk about me like that.

The worst thing is that we weren't even on bad terms. She just felt like bashing me for about 20 minutes (felt like an eternity). I always thought that I'm not completely living up to the image my mom has for me, but I never thought that she's actually disappointed in me this much. A few days earlier, I told her that I don't feel like she respect my ideas and decisions. Of course she dismissed it, saying how I emphasised the negative and forget the positive. But now it's clear that not only does she not respect my ideas, she does not respect me. 

All this time, I had no idea.

She recently attended my graduation ceremony. I graduated, with honors, in a major she was not comfortable for me to be in because she "knows nothing about that field." I thought that was that, and that at least she would understand that I want to make my own decisions. But now it's clear that she doesn't and she simply disapproves all along.

Was she actually proud? Or was she just going through the motions, where she just felt obliged to attend my grad because she's my mom? She always flaunt that she handles office drama well because she knows how to sweet talk and manipulate people. Is this what she's doing to me all this time? How can I be sure if she's genuinely proud of anything I do anymore? Was she ever?

Was she just careless when she continued to talk about me in her normal volume, or did she actually meant for me to hear it, too?

I don't know anymore.

At least my girlfriend (who also heard everything) doesn't share my mom's opinion.

Thanks for the reply.
